video_description:
Bill talks about being sick, Daylight Saving Time messing him up, a Halloween memory he has with Jimmy, their text chain with John Mulaney & Fred Armisen, having to play football growing up because he’s from Oklahoma, his high school yearbook photo, being in the new Netflix Documentary SCTV: The Greatest Show You’ve Never Heard Of, starring in The Cat in the Hat movie, his kids being funny, and doing a guest spot on Abbott Elementary.

About Jimmy Kimmel Live: 
 
Jimmy Kimmel serves as host and executive producer of Emmy® nominated “Jimmy Kimmel Live,” ABC’s late-night talk show. “Jimmy Kimmel Live” is well known for its viral video successes, with over 18 billion views and more than 22 million subscribers on the show’s YouTube channel. Some of Kimmel’s most popular comedy bits include Celebrities Read Mean Tweets, Lie Witness News, Halloween Candy YouTube Challenge, Jimmy and Cousin Sal pranking Aunt Chippy and music stars like Rihanna and Dua Lipa surprising Jimmy in the middle of the night.
brief:
Summary: Bill Hader visits Jimmy Kimmel Live while sick to discuss Daylight Saving Time, a 10-year-old Halloween memory involving a stranded flight in Kentucky with Jimmy Kimmel and Guillermo, their group text chat with John Mulaney and Fred Armisen, his daughters making fun of his texting habits, and his childhood experience playing football in Oklahoma.
People: Bill Hader (guest, actor and comedian); Jimmy Kimmel (host of Jimmy Kimmel Live); John Mulaney (comedian, mentioned as part of group chat); Fred Armisen (actor and comedian, mentioned as part of group chat); Guillermo Rodriguez (talk show sidekick, mentioned in Halloween story); Barry Switzer (former Oklahoma football coach, mentioned regarding football camp)
Context: A late-night talk show interview on Jimmy Kimmel Live following the release/promotion of Bill Hader's projects.
Unclear: The specific illness Bill Hader has (he mentions he cannot talk about it on TV) and the completion of his story regarding whether he was a good football player, as the transcript cuts off at the end.
